#4369. Renault undercuts BYD with a new EV that costs less than $20,000

The new Renault Twingo E-Tech is among the most affordable vehicles, electric or gas-powered, starting at just £14,745 in the UK, or under $20,000.

Another affordable, practical EV the US will never see. Renault’s new Twingo E-Tech is an electric remake of its iconic 1990s city car.

The retro-looking EV went on sale in Europe earlier this year, starting at under €20,000 ($22,000), before government incentives. In places like Germany, it starts at about €13,990 ($15,500), including the €6,000 ($6,600) federal EV grant.

In the UK, Renault announced that prices for the Twingo E-Tech will start at just £14,745, or about $19,500. That includes the government’s Electric Clean Car Grant (ECG) of £3,750 ($4,900).

At that price, Renault’s new electric car is among the most affordable vehicles available, including gas-powered cars.

It’s cheaper than the gas-powered Dacia Sandero (£14,765) and BYD’s cheapest EV, the Dolphin Surf (£18,675). Only a few cars are lower-priced, including the Dacia Spring (£11,990) and Leapmotor T03 (£12,995).

What do you get for the price? At just 3,790 mm (149.2″) long, the electric city car is a bit smaller than the Hyundai Inster and the BYD Dolphin Surf.

For those in the US, that’s even smaller than the first-generation Chevy Bolt EV, which measured 4,145 mm (163.2″) in length.

Despite its compact size, the “cheeky, practical” 5-door city car, as Renault calls it, offers up to 360 liters of boot capacity. It also features independent, sliding 50/50 folding rear seats to haul bigger items like a surfboard.

With up to 50 kW DC fast charging, Renault said the Twingo E-Tech can charge from 15% to 80% in 28 minutes.

The base Renault Twingo E-Tech Evolution, priced from £14,745 ($19,500), uses a 27.5 kWh LFP battery and an 80 hp (60 kW) motor, delivering up to 163 miles of WLTP range.

The entry-level version features 16″ steel wheels, a 7″ driver display, 10″ navigation screen, and ADAS features, including cruise control and lane-keep assist.

Renault will offer three Twingo E-Tech trims in total. The mid-range Techno trim gains 18″ wheels, Google built-in with Renault’s Reno avatar, a reversing camera, automatic climate control, a hands-free key card, One Pedal driving, and heated front seats. It starts at £16,245 ($21,500), including the £3,750 ($4,900) ECG.

With Google built in, drivers can easily find and navigate to charging stations via Google Maps, use Google Gemini AI virtual assistance, or access over 100 apps, including Waze and Amazon Music.

At least this car has some styling unlike the generic box style VW offerings in this category. In this size car I prefer the SUV style of the Dacia Spring for myself, but of course we will never see any of these wonderful cars in the USA.

The top-spec Twingo E-Tech Launch Edition, priced from £17,645 ($23,200), including the £3,750 ($4,900) ECG, adds a suite of ADAS features, including blind-spot warning, rear cross-traffic alert and hands-free parking.

#4368. The 1977 Mazda Cosmo Deserves Better

From the archive: It’s a lot more car than the sales figures would have you believe.

From the April 1977 issue of Car and Driver.

Peel the name tags off the Mazda Cosmo, and it could easily pass for an American car. The two-rotor Wankel is as smooth and vibra­tionless as any V-8, the car is easily as quiet inside as a typical intermediate sedan, and the Cosmo’s body even has the same sort of creaky flexibility that we’ve come to expect of Detroit cars. If we didn’t know better, we might think this was a new subcompact Buick or perhaps a miniature Camaro. Never would we confuse it with a Toyota or Datsun.

The Cosmo is something of a mystery car. It was designed with the United States in mind—a fast, smooth sports coupe for a country that swallowed Datsun Z-cars as fast as the ships could unload them at the ports. But for some reason, the Cosmo never struck the American fancy. Maybe it was the bad publicity heaped on the rotary engine; per­haps the dull colors and unfortunate combi­nation of mag wheels and white-wall tires turned off the sporty-car buyer. And we can’t entirely disregard the thought that a coupe with a Vega silhouette, Oldsmobile waterfall grille, and Plymouth Cricket taillights may sim­ply be the wrong thing to wave in American faces. But whatever the reason, Cosmos tend to languish in the showrooms.

See all results for used cars for sale near 22043

That’s the situation in the U.S. In Japan, the Cosmo is last season’s smash hit, named Car of the Year by one of the country’s auto mag­azines and the next best thing in Tokyo to driving a foreign car. (The Japanese, like many Americans, tend to think that anything imported is probably better and certainly more fun than the made-at-home equivalent). The car looks great in its own neighborhood. It has slightly different—but not much small­er—bumpers and the mandatory mirrors perched out on the front fenders halfway to the headlights. But apart from those two de­tails, the Japanese-market Cosmo looks the same as the one we tend to ignore here.

We humbly submit, at this point, that the Cosmo deserves another look, if for no other reason than it features one commodity in de­cidedly short supply elsewhere—horsepower. This car is quick. The engine is wide awake above 2000 rpm, and it climbs to 7000 with­out a backward glance. Freeways abound with legions of 350 four-barrels that won’t match the Cosmo’s pace. And as amazing as it may seem, none of them can come close to the Mazda’s gas mileage. The 1977 model with the standard five-speed trans­mission has been weaned down to 32 mpg highway and 20 mpg city for a combined rating of 25 mpg in the EPA mileage sweep­stakes. That is excellent economy for a car of this performance level.

While the Cosmo is surprisingly economical, it is by no means austere. The interior offers about the same amount of useful space for four occupants as a Camaro, and the trunk, because it stows its spare more ef­ficiently than the Chevrolet, is at least as good. Yet overall, the Mazda Cosmo is about the same size as a Corvette, actually slightly smaller.

See all results for used cars for sale near 22043

The quality of the interior is also on par with that of Detroit models. The dash is molded vinyl with a minimum of seams, and shows the driver a full complement of instruments set in a field of imitation wood. Velour cloth covers the seats and door panels. There is even a trapezoid opera window to delight the double-knit crowd. And if that doesn’t knock them dead at the Donut Center, show them the wire-spoked steering wheel.

There is just one aspect of the Mazda’s er­satz Detroit personality with which we take is­sue: It’s a smooth-road car. On ribbons of un­broken concrete the Cosmo simply glides along, but when the going gets rough, so does the ride. The front wheels steer notice­ably over bumps, and the suspension travel is limited enough so that the wheels are occa­sionally jerked clear of the road on surfaces that are not really that rough. The balance of the car, particularly on smooth roads, is rea­sonable however.

At least the Cosmo’s ailments are the kind that can be fixed, certainly by a second look at the factory and perhaps even with a few bolt-on aftermarket parts. We would start with the shocks and see what happens. The rotary engine, on the other hand, is just fine as it is. And Mazda provides an incredible warranty—­five years or 75,000 miles—to make sure it stays that way. Nobody can dislike a car that is guaranteed to keep running even after the loan is paid off.

#4367. General Motors Futureliner #7 Has a New Lease On Life. Its Restorers Plan to Use It

After its starring role at the 2026 Retromobile New York show, Matt Katz and Rob Ida have big road trip plans for the 1939 Futureliner.

In 1941, General Motors hit the open road with its fleet of Futureliners on the Parade of Progress, a movement meant to spread cutting-edge science and technology across America. With their bubble-top cockpits, exhibition-style innards, and shining chrome panels, the Futureliners became as much of a spectacle as the displays on automotive technology, urban engineering, farming, and leisure pursuits carried within. Now, 85 years later, a resurrected Futureliner is carrying the Parade of Progress torch into the 21st Century—starting in New York City.

Like many modern automotive stories, this Futureliner's resurrection began on Facebook Marketplace. When Matt Katz, owner of the Caretakers Collection, was sent a link to an available Futureliner on the online classified site, he jumped into action. Katz was on the phone with the seller in a matter of minutes, and quickly deputized friend and New Jersey car builder Rob Ida to travel up to Massachusetts the following day.

“[The seller] was totally caught off guard that I just called him. He's like, ‘Listen, like it's Monday night. I'm out at an event. You know, call me tomorrow.’ I'm like, ‘No, no, no, I want to make this deal now.’ I just wanted to lock it up,” Katz said to Road & Track. He said he informed the seller that he wanted Ida, with whom Katz had done prior restoration projects, to come check out the Futureliner. “I was like, ‘Let me call [Ida] and get him to come out and inspect it within forty-eight hours. And if all is good, I'll wire you the balance. And if all is not, return the money to me, the deposit, and we'll call it even.’”

Ida reported back that the Futureliner example was ripe for restoration, but the journey couldn’t begin immediately. First, Ida had to cut a larger opening in his garage to fit the Futureliner through. Standing 11-feet-7-inches tall and 33 feet long, the GM Futureliner is taller than your average school bus, and about as long as an average fire truck. But once the Futureliner had been transported and maneuvered into Ida’s garage, the real work began.

As it had been owned and restored by the Peter Pan Bus Company in the 1990s, this Futureliner build started out in better shape than most. It had been updated with GM’s post-World War II styling from 1953—a flatter and less regal version of the shape introduced in 1939. Ida and Katz wanted to bring this Futureliner back to its original Harley Earl-designed glory, but there wasn’t an official blueprint to guide them. Ida even reached out to the General Motors Heritage Center, but it had limited information available about the first-generation Futureliner design. So, Ida had to fabricate many of the parts himself. Some era-specific parts even required the creation of bespoke molds, as no replacements were available.

“We work off imagery, and we work off of any kind of text or information that we can find. Unfortunately, the Thirty-Nine version is much more difficult to find than the Fifty-Three version. Anytime you do a quick search, you're going to find all the white roof Fifty-Three generation-two post-war Futureliner. So that was really the difficult part: digging deep enough to find the Thirty-Nine version,” Ida said to Road & Track.

“Somewhere in a conversation with Rob, it came to be that we both agreed: let's go back to the bubble. Let's bring it back to Thirty-Nine, and we didn't realize and truly fully appreciate what that meant. Getting the bubble done was just difficult, but we knew what to do, and Rob had experience,” Katz said. “We didn't realize that after we made that decision, everything else would change on the bus. Not just the paint colors, but also the cladding on the side. So, Fifty-Three has seven clads; ours is four. The GM logo on the front. Rob randomly found this old video by a production company called Rose that I discovered, and he poured through it and discovered in a small clip that the GM logo was backlit.”

Once the restoration was complete, Katz and Ida were eager to show off the piece of moving history, and the inaugural Retromobile event in New York City was the perfect venue. But the newly revived Futureliner had to make it from Old Bridge, New Jersey, to Manhattan’s Jacob K. Javits Convention Center. There is no shortage of driving obstacles between those two points on a good day in a regular car, so piloting the massive machine was sure to be a challenge—but with Ida and Katz at the helm, however, the journey went smoother than expected. Thanks to dually-style front wheels, power steering, 360-degree cameras, and working air conditioning, driving the Futureliner was an exercise in patience more than anything else.

“So I drove from Columbus Circle to Times Square to Javits. And as a New Yorker, driving it in New York and just seeing people's reactions ... you know, part of the enjoyment is how people react to it. I've never had a reaction like when I was driving it. And then the fact that they closed Times Square for me while we were driving, and for Rob and me ... I couldn't even have fathomed that as a dream,” Katz said.

And the Futureliner’s adventures are far from over. Katz and Ida are currently scheming a cross-country road trip, starting on the East Coast in 2027 and heading west toward GM’s Heritage Center in Sterling, Michigan. After that, the Futureliner will head to California for the 2027 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, with stops at dealerships and historical markers along the way. The Futureliner will then spend some time at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles and stick around for the 2028 Summer Olympics before heading back to GM’s Heritage Center. This cross-country journey will be focused on charity efforts for organizations like the Sloan Kettering Institute for Cancer Research, which the original Parade of Progress highlighted. Trust us: if the Futureliner comes to your town, it’s worth seeing in person.

A New York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

#4365. Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

The first post-Stella Montis patch for Arc Raiders has arrived, and it predictably touches much of what people brought to the latest map.

Arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the new “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

#4363. Gordon Ramsay Is the New Host of the BBC’s ‘Top Gear’

The celebrity chef’s run on the legendary car show is set to start airing in 2028.

At one point, Top Gear was one of the biggest shows on television of any sort. It has been a long time since the glory days of Clarkson, Hammond, and May, though, and multiple efforts to revive the BBC’s legendary automotive series have failed to come close to the impact of the original. The show has not been in production since its newest episodes aired in 2022, but a new host is about to change that very soon. On Wednesday, the BBC announced that celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay is taking over the mantle of Top Gear host starting in 2028. Ramsay will be the first host of the show since production paused after a crash involving then-presenter Freddie Flintoff four years ago.

An announcement from the BBC makes no mention of any potential co-hosts alongside Ramsay, but does add that he will be hosting along with “as yet unnamed co-presenters.” The same announcement quotes BBC Studios Entertainment executive Suzy Lamb as saying that the new Top Gear “won't be a nostalgic reboot" and would instead be a “bold and unmissable new chapter” of the show, lines that suggest a major format change could come with the new host.

While Ramsay is most famous for his career as a chef and host of cooking-related shows, he is also a long-time enthusiast who takes his own cars to the track. He even combined the interests back in 2023, cooking a grilled cheese sandwich in the engine bay of his Aston Martin Valkyrie during a track day. This past weekend, he competed in a celebrity race in Lego Formula 1 cars at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Fred Smith's love of cars comes from his fascination with auto racing. Unfortunately, that passion led him to daily drive a high-mileage, first-year Porsche Panamera. He is still thinking about the last lap of the 2011 Indianapolis 500.

#4361. Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen are slashing EV prices by $10,000+ for Black Friday

Forget waiting in line for a discounted TV or other gadget you probably don’t need. If you’ve been looking to go electric, Black Friday may be the time to do it. Several brands, including Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen, are offering $10,000 or more off select EVs right now.

While electric vehicle sales have slowed in the US after last year’s rush of buyers trying to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, the market is bouncing back.

Nearly 263,000 EVs were sold in the US in the third quarter, according to Kelley Blue Book, marking the most since the record-setting third quarter of 2025.

With new models hitting the market, prices have also come down over the past year. The average transaction price (ATP) for a new EV in October was $56,221, down 2.9% from a year ago.

For Black Friday, several automakers are sweetening the deal this year, offering a generous $10,000 or more off select EVs.

Lucid launched its Black Friday offers this week. Through November 30, you can score a $15,000 Black Friday Credit on a new 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring.

Prefer a sedan? Lucid is also offering a $10,000 Black Friday Credit on a new 2027 Lucid Air Touring. To take advantage of the offer, you must pay cash or use third-party financing.

The 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring starts at $79,900 and offers up to 337 miles of EPA-estimated range. It’s available to lease for as low as $749 a month. The offer is for a 36-month lease with $6,249 due at signing.

Lucid’s electric sedan, the 2027 Air Touring, is priced from $79,900 and offers up to 431 miles of range.

Both the Gravity and Air can add up to 200 miles of range in under 12 minutes with 400 kW DC fast charging.

Lucid’s Black Friday offers end on November 30, 2026.

Kia is offering $10,000 off several electric vehicles for Black Friday, including the three-row EV9 and the Niro EV.

The 2026 Kia EV9 is available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount that can be applied toward the purchase price. With a $10,000 discount, prices for the base EV9 Light RWD trim can fall to as low as $44,900 ($54,900 starting MSRP).

Kia is also promoting a lease deal on the 2026 EV9 Light Long Range RWD for $339/month for 36 months, with $4,999 due at signing.

If you opt to finance, you can get 0% APR for 60 months, plus $5,000 in APR Bonus Cash across the entire 2026 EV9 lineup.

The 2026 Kia Niro EV is also available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount, knocking the price down to as low as $29,700 ($39,700 MSRP).

With leases starting at just $289/month for 36 months (with $3,999 due at signing), the 2026 Niro EV Wind FWD is about as cheap a lease as you can get nowadays, gas or electric.

The Niro EV is also available with 0% APR for up to 72 months, including a $3,500 APR Bonus Cash discount.

While it isn’t $10,000 off, it is worth mentioning that Kia now sells the smaller EV3 electric SUV. The 2027 Kia EV3 (see our review) starts at just $28,890, making it one of the most affordable EVs you can get in the US, alongside the new Chevy Bolt and Nissan LEAF.

Kia is offering a $1,500 Customer Cash discount on the 2027 EV3, which still makes it cheaper to buy outright than the Niro EV, even with incentives.

The 2027 Kia EV3 Wind FWD is available for lease starting at $349/month for 36 months, with $3,999 due at signing. Kia is offering 0.90% APR for 48 months on all 2027 EV3 trims.

Kia’s current deals end on January 04, 2027.

#4360. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4359. Can’t Wait for the Scion Kei-01? Grab This Daihatsu HiJet Pickup Now

This kei truck is currently up for auction on Bring a Trailer.

Toyota’s surprising decision to start selling new kei trucks under the Scion brand in the United States as low-speed vehicles (LSVs) has generated a lot of excitement. How could it now? Just look how cute these little trucks are. It’s enough to make you want to drive to Costco and bring home a single large box of cereal tied down in the pint-sized bed.

But why wait for the Scion to get here? Right now, there’s a legally imported keijidosha pickup over at Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos): a 2000 Daihatsu HiJet, which happens to be the same model on which the new Scion is based.

Even if these wee haulers look like they've escaped from the pages of a Richard Scarry book, the kei truck segment is serious business in Japan. Over there, these little pickups work just as hard as larger trucks, carrying a little less cargo but doing the work of road repair, smaller construction projects, plumbing work, and, of course, gardening. For the latter, there's even an annual competition to put together the best bonsai garden in a kei truck bed.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014

On this side of the Pacific, you'll need to carefully check what your state laws say about the use of kei trucks on public roads, as some states allow them to be driven on roads with a speed limit of 35 mph or less, while others only allow them to be used on private property.

Even with those restrictions, this HiJet would be incredibly useful for ferrying around livestock feed on a farm, or shuttling small deliveries around a busy factory complex, or even getting evil minions around a hollowed-out volcano lair. If it does pass muster for on-road use where you live, these trucks are surprisingly plucky to drive, and would make for the ultimate DIY partner. Plenty of hunters and fishermen also appreciate four-wheel-drive kei trucks for their ability to squeeze down narrow tracks where full-size pickups can't go.

The bed is also surprisingly flexible, with fold-down sides that transform it into a mini-flatbed truck. The payload is stouter than you'd think, rated for 770 pounds, so though it may be tiny, it's still mighty.

Daihatsu has plenty of experience building kei trucks and cars, including as a subcontractor for other companies, including Toyota. The HiJet has been around since the 1960s, making it Japan's version of the F-150.

Motive power comes from a 659cc three-cylinder engine plonked in the middle of the chassis, good for a whopping 42 horsepower. That power goes to the rear wheels through a five-speed manual transmission, or you can hit a button and get power to all four corners. The selling dealer has recently replaced the battery and done a mild tune-up, including new spark plugs and an oil change.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014

In short, Scion’s HiJet looks like a fun idea, but this HiJet is ready to get to work right now. The auction ends on November 25.

#4358. Carnegie Mellon’s Buggy Is the 100-Year-Old Race Series You Never Knew About, But Won’t Be Able to Stop Watching

Race pits teams against each other to engineer a new vehicle every year that balances aero, handling, and weight, while enabling a driver to somehow squeeze inside.

Ever heard of Buggy? With a capital B? Referring to a specific type of racing? Neither had we, until recently—but where there’s racing, count Road & Track intrigued. Buggy, so you know, is a unique form of racing only taking place at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU), and it’s been happening for more than 100 years. Similar to Formula SAE, students engineer, build, and drive the vehicles that compete in the odd spectacle. And yes, in case you were questioning how the buggy is driven, someone is actually inside that tube of carbon fiber.

To understand how this sport works from the car design to the track, Road & Track spoke with Caroline Kiesnowski, the head mechanic and driver for a team. Currently a junior in mechanical engineering at CMU, she broke down what it takes to compete in Buggy.

“Basically, the easiest way to describe it is you put a person in a tube, and you use it as a baton in a relay race,” Kiesnowski says. “You get pushed up two hills, you do a free roll where the driver is completely in control—they're steering and everything—and then you get pushed back up three more hills to a finish line.”

It’s incredibly competitive, with lots of teams vying for the win. Just like professional motorsports, each team designs a new buggy every year using experience from years past and new digital tools to refine the vehicle. The priorities are fairly self explanatory: you want the smallest, lightest buggy possible for being pushed up the hill, then for the downhill sections, designing a buggy with the smallest coefficient of drag and wheels with minimal rolling resistance is paramount. Speeds top out around 40 miles per hour, so these little vehicles are positively cruising at their fastest pace—especially considering their pilots are a foot above the pavement.

The students who end up piloting them are highly recruited, Kiesnowski tells me. Each team wants the smallest possible buggy, which means you need a small person to design the buggy’s body around. If you watch how a driver load into their respective buggy, you’ll quickly understand how tight the squeeze is and how much the design is centered around the driver.

While most of the course is straight or mild curves, there’s one rather challenging turn called The Chute. It’s the source of many crashes and spins, and is something students need to design their buggy around every year. Two layouts are widely used: one is the standard trike that positions two wheels in the rear and one in the front; while the other is the reverse trike, which, logically, puts two wheels up front and one in the rear.

They each have their pros and cons, but in general, the standard trike is thought to be a bit dodgier in The Chute. With only one front wheel controlling steering and turning, it’s a simple design, but ergonomics and visibility for the driver can suffer. Meanwhile, the reverse trikes most often use Ackermann-style steering, which increases complexity, but Kiesnowski finds it to be a better design for steering and braking.

“The steering question is interesting because of the nature of buggy,” Kiesnowski said. “It's in a sense, proprietary information; it's historically been super-secret about people talking about their teams. Some teams even have blacked out windshields, like reflective windshields, so you can't see their steering.”

Another challenge for the track is that said track is actually just a road, and it’s mighty bumpy. Kiesnowski recalls that teams in the past even designed suspension to give the trike a better ride, but it’s a rare design choice that adds weight to a structure you’re trying to keep as light as possible. And yes, there is passing, especially in the downhill roll section, so you could end up doing some proper wheel-to-wheel racing. As you’d expect, though, safety is the number one goal in this whole competition, so drivers have helmets, and there are regulations teams have to follow in building their vehicles to ensure the sport is as safe as possible.

As with any good motorsports event, I asked Kiesnowski about teams trying to bend the rules and regulations for an advantage. She declined to offer details, but still said there have indeed been instances of teams looking for an advantage beyond the book. (After all, the grand prize of pride and bragging rights over your peers is a mighty tempting trophy in college.)

The competition takes place every April at Carnegie Mellon’s campus in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. And while the engines are essentially members of the team pushing, it’s still a form of racing we can get excited about.

#4357. This 500 kWh energy storage system runs on retired EV batteries

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s new Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment says its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

“We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” said Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Moment Energy says Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

That matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

#4356. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4355. VW’s ID.Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Is a Track-Focused EV

The Clubsport concept turns the practical ID.Polo GTI into a two-door track car—complete with a roll bar, bucket seats, and five-point harnesses.

The Volkswagen GTI badge has been a staple in automotive culture for 50 years, and it’s clearly not getting sidelined anytime soon. VW just released the ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept, an electric track-focused GTI that slots in as the automaker’s fourth new GTI variant this year.

While it’s not heading to production, the Clubsport concept is a peek into the possibilities riding on the electric ID.Polo GTI, which became the first EV to wear the GTI badge when it was released earlier this year. The standard ID.Polo GTI, which isn’t sold in the United States, reaches 62 mph in 6.8 seconds thanks to a 223-hp electric motor mounted to the front axle.

See all results for Volkswagen ID.GTI for sale near 21014

The Clubsport concept ups the ante, with VW claiming it will hit 62 mph in just 4.7 seconds with the help of launch control and a more powerful APP550 electric motor. The upgraded motor, which is typically used to power the rear wheels of larger models like the ID.Tiguan and ID.7, sends 362 horsepower to the front wheels and nearly doubles the standard electric GTI’s torque output from 213 to 406 pound-feet.

Volkswagen also equipped the concept vehicle with an electronically regulated front differential lock, a performance-tuned adaptive suspension system, and ceramic brakes with a one-box brake setup. The high-performance powertrain fits into an equally aggressive two-door build, complete with a large front splitter, diffuser, and a flared rear wing.

Rather than the typical five-seater setup, the Clubsport concept houses two Recaro bucket seats with red five-point harnesses. A Tornado Red roll bar replaces the rear seats, and the cockpit is solely reserved for racing needs, meaning the standard infotainment system is also omitted. The cabin is finished in a dark microfiber material and trimmed with red stitching.

Volkswagen calls this concept the “perfect match of heritage and future,” and the automaker says its young employees were involved in much of the concept’s realization. The ID.Polo GTI Clubsport concept won’t ever make it to VW showrooms, but it’ll be displayed next week at the Essen Motor Show in Essen, Germany.

#4354. BYD offers a first look at its new flagship people mover

BYD is preparing to launch a new flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the new flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A new creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo said after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

The new flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously said the company expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview shows a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD said earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo said to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

#4352. Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale Is the Purest Prancing Horse in Years

The 296 CS adds serious aero and ditches the GTB's hybrid system for a more enthusiast-focused driving experience.

Nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello. A few months ago, Ferrari unveiled the 12Cilindri Manuale, reintroducing a (simulated) six-speed manual transmission to its model lineup purely for the sake of driver involvement. And now, the Challenge Stradale badge returns to the rear engine mesh of a Prancing Horse for the first time since the 360 CS was discontinued in 2004. Simply put, it's a good year to be a sentimental Ferrarista.

In the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year. Parked side by side at their reveal at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya today, we would excuse a gentleman driver for confusing the CS with his new track-only machinery.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 21014

There have been several limited-edition, track-focused mid-engine Ferraris since the 360 Challenge Stradale—including the F430 Scuderia, 458 Speciale, and 488 Pista—but the 296 Challenge Stradale goes the furthest of all of them in emulating its racecar counterpart, both aesthetically and mechanically.

While previous track-centric Ferraris have been somewhat demurely styled, the 296 CS puts its aerodynamic elements on full display. The carbon-fiber rear wing, dive planes, adjustable front splitter, and vented hood are essentially a copy-paste job from the Challenge Evo, with concessions made for road legality. Up front, twin vents positioned in the hood just before the windshield channel hot air expelled from two under-hood radiators over the windshield and towards the rear of the car, reducing the aerodynamic variations caused by changing ground clearance.

Other aero features are hidden out of sight. The CS's underbody has been smoothed to better feed the rear diffuser and work with three pairs of vortex generators at the front and two at the rear to generate additional downforce. With all of the aerodynamic elements colluding, the 296 Challenge Stradale makes 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. That's a 72-percent increase over the base 296GTB's peak figure.

Big changes have been made to the CS's powertrain. You won't find any orange high-voltage wiring snaking around under the glass of its mid-mounted hood like you would in a 296GTB or 296 Speciale, as the 5-kWh battery pack and rear-mounted axial-flux electric motor have been removed entirely. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 operates unassisted and supposedly sounds better than ever courtesy of a reworked twin-exit exhaust system.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 21014

Overall firepower has decreased to 670 horsepower—149 ponies less than the standard 296GTB's. The upside is a notable decrease in mass, with Ferrari claiming that the removal of the plug-in-hybrid componentry played a major role in shedding 328 pounds from the 296GTB's dry weight. A lightened transmission flex plate, driveshaft, and timing cover were also developed to make the CS's powertrain as featherweight as possible. Without an electric motor present to fill in any thrust gaps left by turbo lag, the V-6 has been retuned to increase low-end grunt, although peak torque remains 546 pound-feet delivered at 6250 rpm.

As to be expected, yanking out an integrated powertrain system comes with some unique challenges that affect more than just the engine itself. For example, Ferrari was forced to enlarge the 296 CS's rear carbon-ceramic brake rotors and the ventilation ducts that cool them to compensate for the lack of regenerative braking. The decreased weight in the rear also shifted its weight distribution 1.5 percent to the front, which was addressed with suspension design and geometry changes.

The CS's newly developed suspension is derived directly from the 296 Challenge Evo and features semi-active dampers and a dual-spring design that improves rebound response. The result is reduced body roll, which helps the performance of the specially developed Pirelli P Zero R and P Zero Trofeo RS tires, measuring 245/35ZR-20 in the front and 305/35ZR-20 in the rear. The 20-inch forged wheels can be ordered in Matte Grigio Corsa, Matte Nero with a diamond-cut finish, or Matte Bianco Fuji.

The 296 Challenge Stradale's cockpit is very similar to the one found in the 296 Speciale. While niceties like climate control and a stereo remain, carbon-fiber door panels and a lack of armrests and storage pockets are a clear indication of the CS's weight-saving mission. For true gluttons for punishment, an even further stripped interior spec is available that removes the trim from the area beneath the seats and the lower section of the carpets beneath the center console, leaving part of the chassis exposed.

Ferrari is adamant that the 296 CS isn't a replacement for the 296 Speciale and will not cannibalize that model's customer base, as the two are intended for different buyers. Besides being geared less towards outright track duty, the 296 Speciale is a part of Ferrari's special series, meaning that customers need to have an "existing relationship" with the brand in order to get an allocation. The 296 Challenge Stradale is a standard range model, meaning anyone can walk into a dealer and order one, existing relationship or not. Ferrari says that it wants to court new Ferrari buyers interested in experiencing the purest driving experience that the prancing horse has to offer, and the 296 CS is the first step in that direction.

U.S. pricing has not been announced, but in its home market, the 296 Challenge Stradale costs 291,000 euros, or the equivalent of about $320,000. Stateside deliveries of the new CS are expected to begin sometime in late 2027. As a non-Speciale model, CS production numbers aren’t limited, which presents a unique opportunity to buy a special new Ferrari without already owning one.

#4351. Elon Musk freezes at awkward Tesla Argentina launch: ‘I don’t know what to say’

Tesla officially launched in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

The launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.

Musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”

JAJAJAJ QUE ES ESTO, Milei lo llamó de sorpresa a Elon Musk para que diga algo sobre el local de Tesla inaugurado y es lo mas INCÓMODO que vas a ver en tu vida, se quería ir a la mierda y COLGÓ, durísimo, ni Elon Musk lo soporta al gordo pelotudo pic.twitter.com/CrJkv4iu1x

Then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he said. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil company YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”

And that was it. The feed cut before he even said goodbye.

Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”

The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.

Tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:

Tesla adds about $600 in reservation, destination, and documentation fees on top of that, and first deliveries aren’t expected until March or April 2027. There are no dealers. Sales happen online, with showroom space at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls in Buenos Aires.

Argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which launched in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.

What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating "I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means" in his interview with CNBC.

Especially surprising after he declared, "I’m not just MAGA; I’m 'Dark MAGA,'" after spending half a billion dollars to support MAGA candidates, and after promoting the MAGA political agenda (which he has, in part, personally implemented through the DOGE).

At this point, I expect him to reappear in the guise of a Democrat and write a big, fat, one-billion-dollar check to a Democratic super PAC for the 2028 election cycle.

I am sure Musk has a lot on his mind right now, but selling Tesla vehicles clearly isn’t one of them, because he couldn’t come up with anything to say about it.

Launching a new market has one job: get people excited to buy the cars. Musk had a sitting president cheering for him on stage, a room full of fans, and every camera in Buenos Aires pointed at him. He couldn’t come up with a single reason to buy a Model Y.

This isn’t stage fright. Musk has been telling investors for two years that Tesla’s future is robotaxis and Optimus robots, not selling cars. Meanwhile, Tesla’s deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025, its second annual decline in a row. The guy who is behind the brand doesn’t care about selling these cars anymore, and this clip shows it better than anything I’ve seen.

#4350. Dragon boy Durin is the star of the show in Genshin Impact's wintry Luna 3 update, launching in early December

Genshin Impact is getting two new characters and a whole host of new content in Version Luna 3, which arrives in under two weeks.

The latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us big Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The new chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain new powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a big new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

#4349. Hyundai Ioniq 5 Maintenance Guide: What Needs Servicing And What Doesn’t

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

It’s no secret that electric cars are more affordable to maintain than their gasoline-powered counterparts. While they may have a higher purchase price than a comparable gas-powered vehicle, EVs can save owners money over time by eliminating the need for regular engine oil changes, emissions tests, and other traditional maintenance tasks. Affordable electric vehicles are also becoming increasingly common, with even more options expected to arrive in the coming years.

However, that doesn't mean electric cars are completely maintenance-free. Like any other vehicle, EVs require regular care and attention to remain reliable and perform at their best for many years.

Although they don't have conventional combustion engines or traditional automatic transmissions, electric cars still feature components that require periodic maintenance. These include reduction gearboxes, brake fluid, brake pads, coolant systems, and tires among other things. Keeping these components in good condition is essential to ensuring an EV's long-term reliability.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

For the second installment of our EV maintenance series, I'll be taking a closer look at the Hyundai Ioniq 5, one of the most recognizable electric crossovers on the market. Made in the United States and South Korea, the Ioniq 5 has long been one of the biggest rivals to the ubiquitous Tesla Model Y.

I'll break down Hyundai's recommended maintenance schedule, explaining which items are required to keep the vehicle running smoothly over the long term.

Compared to Tesla, which is known for its rather skimpy maintenance plan, Hyundai includes a generous list of maintenance items in the owner’s manual. The automaker also includes additional service actions that should be performed if the car is used in harsher-than-normal conditions, so owners know what to expect in the long run.

There’s a normal maintenance schedule and a separate section for severe usage and low mileage conditions. Hyundai also has a list of maintenance items that can be performed by the owner. I’ll go through all of them, so drivers can easily mark down what needs to be done during the car’s lifetime.

Hyundai says that normal driving conditions include distances longer than 10 miles, clean roads without salt or dust, ambient temperatures under 90ºF (32ºC), no towing, no roof rack, and normal speeds. Under these conditions, the required maintenance for a Hyundai Ioniq 5 is as follows, according to the owner’s manual:

According to Hyundai, extra precaution needs to be taken if the car is driven under certain conditions. These include repeated driving short distances of less than five miles in normal temperatures or less than 10 miles in freezing temperatures, and driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, graveled, or salt-spread roads.

But that’s not all. Driving in areas using salt or other corrosive materials, or in very cold weather, driving in heavy dust conditions, driving in heavy traffic areas with the ambient temperature higher than 90ºF (32 ºC) while consuming more than 50% of electric energy, and driving on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads repeatedly can also result in extra maintenance items.

Towing a trailer, using a roof rack, driving as a patrol car or taxi, frequently driving at high speeds, and frequently driving in stop-and-go conditions are also part of the conditions that lead to more intense servicing requirements.

In addition to the normal maintenance schedule above, Hyundai recommends the following actions for severe usage and low-mileage conditions:

All of these items should be performed by a Hyundai technician, but the Ioniq 5 also has a consistent list of maintenance actions that should be performed by the owner.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is one of the best-selling electric crossovers in the United States, and for good reason. Its unique styling has plenty of fans, and it’s a genuinely nice car to drive. As for its maintenance requirements, the official recommendations have a lot more items compared to the Tesla Model Y, but at the end of the day, most of them are just inspection jobs. As a result, maintenance costs should be quite low compared to a comparable gas vehicle. Just rotate and replace tires, keep an eye on your brakes, and swap out the coolant after 10 years or 120,000 miles.

#4348. BMW Classic Pulls the Wraps off a Secret 1997 M7 Prototype

Along with a six-speed manual, this one-off features a 400-hp 4.9-liter V-8 from the E39 M5.

At the end of Raiders of the Lost Ark, a nameless government employee wheels the crated-up Ark of the Covenant into a vast and anonymous warehouse, forever to be lost again. You have to imagine this is like what going to work in BMW’s mechanical archives is like, where hidden wonders wait patiently to see the light of day again.

Well, here’s something to melt your face right off: the secret prototype M7 BMW never made. Powered by the 4.9-liter V-8 that would go on to make the E39 M5 such a legend, it's a manual-transmission 1997 short-wheelbase E38 7-series, a total wolf in sheep’s clothing.

Rated at the same 400 horsepower as the later M5 would have, this car was only just revealed by BMW’s Classic division. As a prototype, it’s quite the what-might-have-been story, although BMW probably wasn’t all that serious about producing a full M version of its luxury flagship. Instead, the V-12-powered 750iL that Pierce Brosnan pilots remotely from the back seat in 1997's Tomorrow Never Dies provided plenty of drama.

See all results for BMW 7-series for sale near 21014

However, the idea of a roomy limousine-class sedan with M5 power certainly gets the imagination going. BMW financed a series of films in the early 2000s featuring Clive Owen as a nameless driver, collected together as The Hire, and the one Guy Ritchie directed featured Owen ferrying Madonna around at breakneck speed in an M5. This M7 prototype would have worked just as well.

Besides the powertrain, a big part of this prototype’s appeal is just how understated it is. BMW’s M division doesn’t really do subtlety much anymore—customers want their carbon-fiber accents and M badges—but this black sedan would have flown completely under the radar in 1997. Engineers out testing it on the unrestricted autobahns must have had a heck of a time.

Sadly, like the E31-chassis, V-12-powered M8 prototype, the M7 would never make its way to a production version. Perhaps, though, that makes it all the more appealing, a secret treasure that’s been kept out of view, now finally breaking cover again. Dr. Jones might argue that it belongs in a museum. We’d sure like to slide behind the wheel and see if this one-off M7 will hit its stated top speed of 155 mph.

#4347. Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

Electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.

It’s a big change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.

I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it launched on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.

The game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.

That changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.

That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in big, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.

That last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing. Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.

GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.

Rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.

Kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.

And finding a charger isn’t a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations.

Rockstar’s EV history starts with Coil, the series’ Tesla stand-in, named after the Tesla coil. GTA V, released in 2013, gave us the Coil Voltic, a copy of the original Lotus-based Tesla Roadster, alongside oddballs like the Cheval Surge and the Fisker Karma-inspired Khamelion.

The Voltic was quick off the line and slow everywhere else. It had the lowest top speed of any supercar in the game, which fan lore pins on its battery overheating at speed. That’s pretty much how a lot of people thought about EVs in 2013.

GTA Online added more electric cars starting in late 2017: the Rimac-inspired Coil Cyclone, then the Model S-based Coil Raiden and the Taycan-inspired Pfister Neon around the Doomsday Heist update. That same update introduced Avon Hertz, a tech billionaire whose AI tries to end the world. Rockstar never said who he was based on. Players didn’t need the help.

But those were rare, expensive toys. Nothing in GTA V needed fuel, so an EV was just a gas car without the engine noise, and you mostly saw them in the garages of players who bought them.

Electrify America noticed its in-game twin fast. The Volkswagen-owned network put out a statement on Friday saying it “will stick to charging vehicles in the real world” and adding, “We wish ReVolt America well.”

It’s a good-natured response, and probably the best free marketing the network has had in years. EA has spent most of the last decade fighting a reputation for broken chargers, even though reliability across US fast-charging networks has improved this year. Every ReVolt station I’ve used in the game worked. Not a perfect parody, then.

GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it’s now slightly ahead of it.

Florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of new passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy. Electrify America alone runs more than 350 chargers at over 60 Florida stations, including its biggest station yet near Orlando’s theme parks.

But real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation’s count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap’s count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio.

There’s one piece Rockstar hasn’t nailed, at least not yet. You can’t install a charger at your place, but early in the story you’re renting. I’m not far enough in to own a property, so I don’t know whether that changes later.

It matters, because home charging is the biggest real-world advantage of an EV. Most owners leave every morning with a full battery and rarely use public chargers. If owned properties in GTA 6 come with a plug, EVs become the more convenient choice in the game, just like they are in real life for anyone with a driveway.

I also haven’t hit a mission built around EVs yet. If I find one, I’ll update this post.

GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it’s just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall.

That’s a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what’s common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience. Take-Two says GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that.

So EVs aren’t a statement in GTA anymore. They’re normal, which is exactly the point the industry has been trying to make for years.

#4346. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

Elon loves to mash his companies together. He claims the Roadster has boosters from SpaceX, and the Cybercab has Starlink internet. And its coming to more Teslas, Musk said Monday. This came in response to X user David Marcus, who said: "Can't wait for Tesla to offer an embedded Starlink option on all models (beyond the Cybercab)."

Elon's timelines are about as reliable as mine when I tell my wife I'm gonna mow the lawn on Football Sunday. However, the technology already seems like it's there with the Cybercab, and the patent is already filed. It's just a matter of integrating it into existing models.
